attacks.claim: The public Recent signers panel shows full name and postal code, which violates the agreed rule that public signer lists show at most first name, last initial and city. Once published, this exposure cannot be retracted.
attacks.evidence: • {{ s.full_name }} {{ s.city }} {{ s.postal_code }}

attacks.claim: The newsletter/organizer-updates checkbox is pre-ticked. Pre-ticked opt-in is not valid GDPR consent for EU signers (Art. 4(11), Art. 7) and is non-compliant for email marketing under ePrivacy/PECR. The rollout would send unlawful marketing consent to EU residents.
attacks.evidence: <input type="checkbox" id="news" name="newsletter_opt_in" value="1" checked>

attacks.claim: Organizer news emails have no stated unsubscribe mechanism, no stated controller/processor role for the organizer, and no lawful-basis statement. CSV export of signer emails to organizers is also not covered by any data-sharing terms.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: unsubscribe flow, controller/processor roles for organizer updates and CSV export, lawful basis for organizer news

attacks.claim: Confirmation emails go to Postmark, a US processor, for EU signers. The transfer mechanism (SCCs/TIA) is not stated; the artifact only says a DPA was countersigned.
attacks.evidence: Confirmation emails go through Postmark; DPA countersigned 2026-09-14, listed in the public subprocessor page.

attacks.claim: Duplicate-email rejection with 409 lets anyone probe whether a given email has signed a given petition, which is a membership/linkability leak for political-participation data.
attacks.evidence: Duplicate signature (same email) rejected with 409

attacks.claim: No retention period or erasure path is defined for confirmed signatures (name, email, postal code). Only unconfirmed signatures have a purge rule, so GDPR storage limitation and Art. 17 erasure requests cannot be honoured.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: retention period for confirmed signatures; erasure/access request process. Only: unconfirmed signatures are purged after 7 days.

attacks.claim: Data residency is keyed to the postal code, not to the data subject's location. EU residents abroad, or non-EU residents with EU-resolved codes, are routed incorrectly, and backups/replicas are not addressed. Single-vendor email (Postmark) has no stated exit path.
attacks.evidence: eu-central-1 for EU-resolved postal codes, us-east-1 otherwise

attacks.claim: The sign endpoint has no CSRF token, rate limiting or bot protection. Arbitrary third-party email addresses can be submitted, triggering unsolicited confirmation emails and abuse of the sender reputation.
attacks.evidence: <form class="sign-form" action="/p/{{ petition.slug }}/sign" method="post" novalidate> (no CSRF field); ABSENT: rate limit on /sign and confirmation sends

attacks.claim: Organizer CSV export contains user-controlled names and emails with no formula-injection neutralisation. Values starting with =, +, - or @ can execute as formulas when opened in spreadsheet software.
attacks.evidence: Organizers can export signers who opted in to updates as CSV; export is rate-limited and audit-logged. ABSENT: CSV formula escaping

attacks.claim: sign.js handles only 422 and ok. A 409 duplicate, a 5xx or a network error produces no visible message, because the form-error paragraph is never populated. Users see a silent failure. A missing Location header also sets window.location to null.
attacks.evidence: if (res.status === 422) {...} if (res.ok) window.location = res.headers.get('Location'); /

attacks.claim: Invalid fields are indicated only by red border and background colour. There is no text error message, no aria-invalid, and the aria-live region is never filled, so screen-reader users get no error identification (WCAG 1.4.1, 3.3.1).
attacks.evidence: .sign-form input.is-invalid { border: 2px solid #d93025; background: #fdecea; } /

attacks.claim: WCAG 2.1 AA compliance is claimed from an automated axe-core scan alone, which cannot verify keyboard flow, focus order, error identification or screen-reader behaviour. No manual AT testing is listed. The QA row 'Recent signers renders 20 most recent confirmed: Pass' also contradicts the agreed first-name/last-initial/city rule.
attacks.evidence: axe-core automated scan on sign page | 0 violations  /  Recent signers renders 20 most recent confirmed | Pass

attacks.claim: Load testing covers only 400 signatures/s. It does not cover concurrent viewers polling every 15s or the per-page recent_signers query under 10-100x traffic. A surge on a viral petition is untested.
attacks.evidence: Load: 400 signatures/s sustained for 10 min, p95 210ms  /  Signature counts update live (polling every 15s, cached at the CDN for 10s).

attacks.claim: The rollback (flag off) does not reverse what has already happened: names and postal codes already shown publicly, CDN/crawler caches, and emails already sent under pre-ticked consent. The plan has no remediation or purge step for the 10% cohort.
attacks.evidence: Rollback: flip petitions_signing off; sign form is replaced by the existing 'Follow this petition' button.

attacks.claim: Monitoring covers submit errors and bounces only. It has no alert for 409 spikes, PII exposure, or consent-related metrics. The 24h watch window is shorter than the 7-day purge cycle, so purge failures would go unseen.
attacks.evidence: Watch sign_submit_error_rate (< 0.5%) and confirmation email bounce rate (< 2%) for 24h.

attacks.claim: Confirmation emails are sent per submission with no per-petition or per-IP quota. Bot signing could run up Postmark spend without a cap.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: send quota or budget cap for confirmation emails

attacks.claim: The consent copy 'and others from {{ organizer.name }}' is vague about what the signer is opting into. Required fields carry no visible required indicator.
attacks.evidence: Keep me updated about this campaign and others from {{ petition.organizer.name }}

attacks.claim: novalidate disables native validation and the error path depends on JavaScript. Without JS, the form has no working validation feedback.
attacks.evidence: <form class="sign-form" ... novalidate>

attacks.claim: Client code assumes server-returned field names exist in the form, and fields[0] is read without a guard. An empty or unknown fields array throws a TypeError. Validation logic is duplicated between client and server with no shared contract.
attacks.evidence: for (const name of fields) form.elements[name].classList.add('is-invalid'); form.elements[fields[0]].focus();

attacks.claim: No gate-blocking value concern: the signing flow and momentum panel match the stated goal. The residual risk sits in the privacy and consent findings above.
attacks.evidence: Public 'Recent signers' panel on each petition page showing first name + last initial and city, so visitors can see momentum without exposing signers.

attacks.claim: Rollout proceeds to 100% on Friday after only 24h at 10%, with no explicit go/no-go gate tied to privacy or consent sign-off.
